issues.t: Automatic shifts erratically or drops into neutral
issues.sym: Harsh or delayed shifts, the gear display flashing or showing a D with a line through it, trouble getting out of Park, or the transmission suddenly dropping into neutral, sometimes at highway speed.
issues.why: Many owners trace this to the transmission range sensor (the switch that tells the computer which gear is selected) or its wiring connector. Some report the problem coming back after the sensor was replaced.
issues.next: If the car drops into neutral or loses drive, signal, move out of traffic and stop. Have the transmission codes read (P0700 and P0705 are common) and the range sensor and its connector checked before replacing the transmission.

issues.t: Engine loses power or stalls while driving
issues.sym: The car suddenly will not accelerate, revs without picking up speed, or stalls in traffic. A check engine light may come on.
issues.why: Owners report stalling and loss of power tied to throttle body or throttle sensor faults and to transmission range sensor problems. Some cars needed a computer software update from the dealer.
issues.next: Treat sudden power loss as a safety issue: get out of traffic and stop. Have codes read and ask a dealer about any software updates for your VIN.

issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, coolant keeps disappearing, white exhaust smoke, or a rough-running engine.
issues.why: Head gasket failures are among the most reported Forenza engine problems, usually at 80,000-100,000 miles, and often show up after an overheating episode.
issues.next: If the engine overheats, pull over and shut it off right away. Have a cooling system pressure test and a combustion leak test done before the engine is damaged further.

issues.t: Timing belt breaks and damages the engine
issues.sym: The engine suddenly quits while driving and then cranks but will not start.
issues.why: The 2.0L engine uses a rubber timing belt and is an interference design, so when the belt breaks the valves and pistons collide. Owners report belts breaking and needing head rebuilds or a replacement engine; a failing water pump can take the belt with it.
issues.next: If you do not have a record of a timing belt change, have the belt and water pump replaced now. If the belt has already broken, do not keep cranking the engine; have a shop check for valve damage.

issues.t: Headlight switch or DRL module can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Headlights or daytime running lights act up, a hot or burning-plastic smell near the left side of the steering column, or a melted switch.
issues.why: Heat builds up in the headlight switch or the daytime running light module, which can melt the part and create a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Suzuki dealers replace the switch, add a relay kit and replace the DRL module free. If you smell burning plastic, stop and turn the car off.

issues.t: Headlights cut out from melted wiring splice (recall)
issues.sym: Low beams, high beams or daytime running lights flicker or stop working.
issues.why: A poor connection in a wiring splice pack for the headlight power circuit heats up and melts. Suzuki recalled the cars twice for this, once in 2007 and again in 2012.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls; the repair is free. Do not drive at night without working headlights.

issues.t: Front seat belt buckle may not latch (recall)
issues.sym: The front seat belt will not latch, or it releases unexpectedly.
issues.why: Suzuki recalled these cars because the front seat belt buckle can malfunction.
issues.next: Check the recall status with your VIN. Have any buckle that does not click firmly fixed before carrying passengers in that seat.

issues.sym: The brake lights stay on when you are not braking, the battery runs down, or cruise control acts up.
issues.why: A faulty brake light switch can keep the brake lights on all the time, so drivers behind you cannot tell when you brake.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the switch repair is free. Have someone confirm your brake lights work normally.

issues.sym: Usually no warning. The airbag light may come on.
issues.why: Suzuki recalled some early Forenzas because the driver airbag might not deploy correctly in a frontal crash.
issues.next: Confirm with a Suzuki dealer that this recall was completed on your car.

issues.sym: The airbag light stays on or keeps coming back after it is reset.
issues.why: Owners report faults in the airbag control module, the passenger seat occupant sensor and wiring under the seats.
issues.next: While this light is on the airbags may not work. Have the airbag codes read by a shop with the right scan tool.

issues.t: Hard starting or no-start, fixed by software update
issues.sym: The engine will not start or will not turn over, often after sitting overnight or in cold weather, sometimes on almost new cars.
issues.why: Some owners say the dealer traced it to engine computer programming and installed updated software.
issues.next: Ask a Suzuki dealer or a shop with dealer-level software whether an engine computer update applies to your car.

issues.t: Oil pressure light and sudden oil loss
issues.sym: The oil pressure light comes on while driving, sometimes with oil sprayed under the hood.
issues.why: A few owners report a sudden loss of oil pressure that led to major engine repairs. The cause varies from car to car.
issues.next: If the oil light comes on, pull over and shut off the engine right away. Check the oil level and have the car towed if it is low or leaking.

issues.sym: The clutch pedal goes soft or to the floor and you cannot shift gears.
issues.why: On manual cars the hydraulic slave cylinder that releases the clutch can leak or fail. Owners report this failure.
issues.next: Have the clutch hydraulics checked. Replacing the clutch at the same time can save labor if it is worn.

issues.t: Electrical faults with gauges, windows or locks
issues.sym: Gauges flicker, power windows or locks stop working, or warning lights come on at random.
issues.why: Electrical system complaints are among the most common for these years.
issues.next: Have a shop check the battery, grounds and fuses first, then trace the circuit that is acting up.

issues.t: Check engine light from oxygen sensor (P0133)
issues.sym: Check engine light on with code P0133.
issues.why: The upstream oxygen sensor slows down with age and the engine computer flags it.
issues.next: Have the code confirmed. Replacing the sensor usually clears it.

issues.sym: Oil seeping on top of the engine, or a burning-oil smell after driving.
issues.why: The rubber valve cover gasket hardens and leaks oil.
issues.next: Replace the gasket before oil reaches the spark plug wells or hot exhaust.

issues.t: Inside door handles break or lose paint
issues.sym: Interior door handles pop off or break, or the paint peels off the handles.
issues.why: Owners report weak door handle parts and finishes that wear quickly.
issues.next: Replace a broken handle soon; a door that cannot be opened from inside is a problem in an emergency.

issues.sym: The radio display goes blank or stops working.
issues.why: The display on the factory radio fails on some cars.
issues.next: A shop or car audio installer can repair or replace the radio.
